principle_text: When the seller reiterates interest in selling without addressing the price, avoid focusing on product details like carrier compatibility that do not directly contribute to price negotiation.
When the seller emphasizes the excellent condition of the item without addressing pricing, avoid asking questions that do not directly push for a lower price or negotiate terms.

When the seller indicates the item is in like-new condition and suitable for all carriers, avoid offering a significantly lower price than their initial asking price to prevent weakening your negotiation leverage.
When the seller confirms an included accessory, avoid failing to link it to price concessions, as it may leave the negotiation dynamics unchanged and miss an opportunity for leverage.
When the seller offers a counteroffer higher than the buyer's initial proposal, avoid accepting without further negotiation to maintain leverage and seek a better deal.
When the seller has already accepted your offer and finalized the price, avoid confirming pickup arrangements as it does not provide an opportunity for further negotiation or leverage.
When the buyer challenges the seller's initial price and refuses to negotiate, avoid directly rejecting the offer and escalating the price significantly in response.
When the seller's initial price is challenged by the buyer, clarify and confirm the original price to maintain transparency and prevent price escalation.
When the seller agrees to a lower price without pushback, you should leverage factors like inspecting the item in person to secure a better deal.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition, avoid introducing factors that could justify a lower price, as it may strengthen the buyer's position in negotiations.
When the buyer introduces a competitive benchmark to justify a lower offer, you should consider adjusting your price to align with market references and strengthen your position in the negotiation.
When the seller immediately agrees to a price offer, you should strategically close the price gap and prompt a favorable response by proposing a slightly higher but still reasonable counteroffer.

When the buyer asserts a significantly lower price target than the seller's offer, the seller should consider making a counteroffer with a slight reduction while introducing minor concessions to maintain negotiation momentum.

When the seller has agreed to reduce the price to $18 upon pickup, avoid passively accepting the offer without further negotiation or challenging for a lower price to maintain leverage in the negotiation.

When the seller has already agreed to a price, avoid attempting to renegotiate without presenting a specific counteroffer, as it can create unnecessary uncertainty and weaken your position in the negotiation.

When the seller emphasizes the item's excellent condition and included accessories, avoid failing to negotiate terms directly and conceding on price, as it maintains the item's perceived worth without altering leverage.
When the seller firmly states their minimum price, you should avoid proposing counteroffers significantly lower than their minimum to maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller lowers the price and offers additional items in response to buyer's leverage on product limitations, you should continue to emphasize the product's drawbacks to secure a better deal.
When the seller explicitly states they don't need a non-cash item, avoid introducing irrelevant items in negotiation to prevent weakening your leverage and maintain focus on price discussions.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate by lowering the price, you should continue exploring alternative items for trade to maintain pressure and improve your bargaining position.
When the seller offers a counter price with additional items, avoid accepting without further negotiation to prevent conceding ground and weakening your leverage in the negotiation.
When the seller has already stated their minimum price, avoid making lower offers that do not meet their stated threshold, as it weakens your negotiating position.
When the seller discloses minor scratches and the absence of included accessories, you should leverage this information to negotiate a lower price effectively.

When the seller shows willingness to negotiate and offers additional accessories, avoid making offers below the current negotiation range to maintain leverage and prevent the seller from increasing the price.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate and offers additional accessories, avoid accepting the counteroffer immediately without exploring further price reduction.

When the seller has already accepted a final price and terms, avoid making responses that do not engage in further price negotiation or leverage-building, as it does not impact obtaining a better deal.
When the seller expresses willingness to negotiate, you should continue to push for a lower price to leverage this openness and work towards a better deal.

When the seller is willing to negotiate and offers a counter price, you should start with an aggressive anchor below the seller's initial asking price to establish leverage and narrow the negotiation range in your favor.
When the seller has already offered a lower price and additional product information, you should demonstrate flexibility and negotiate in person with a cash offer to secure a better deal.
When the seller indicates openness to negotiation after a price inquiry, you should propose a specific lower offer to advance the bargaining process.
When the seller signals willingness to negotiate but sets a firm minimum price, avoid making offers significantly lower than your initial stated price as it may weaken your bargaining position.
When the seller firmly states a minimum price and introduces additional conditions, avoid conceding too much too quickly as it weakens your negotiating leverage without securing a better deal.
When the seller firmly states a minimum acceptable price without offering concessions, avoid asking questions that do not directly challenge the price or introduce new negotiation leverage.
When the seller states a firm minimum price, you should meet that price and add a value-adding condition to secure agreement and improve your deal.
When the seller clearly agrees to your target price without resistance, you should confirm the agreed price promptly to finalize the deal efficiently.
When the seller makes a counteroffer above the buyer's initial price, avoid immediately accepting without attempting further negotiation to maximize price concessions.

When the seller states a high initial price and highlights product features, you should anchor your offer firmly and challenge the seller to justify a higher price to gain leverage and prompt concessions.

When the seller has made a firm counteroffer above your initial price, avoid raising your offer while simultaneously issuing an ultimatum, as it reduces your leverage and weakens your negotiating position.
When the seller counters with a firm price but is open to pickup arrangements, you should offer a lower price combined with convenient pickup and additional small incentives to encourage acceptance.
When the seller agrees to a lower price and pickup terms, you should promptly confirm acceptance to finalize the deal and secure the negotiated price.

When the seller firmly states a minimum acceptable price and justifies it, avoid increasing your offer too close to that minimum without additional leverage, as it may weaken your negotiating position.
When the seller offers additional value to justify a higher price, avoid immediately accepting add-ons without further negotiating the price to maintain leverage.

When the seller responds with a firm but reduced price offer including conditions, you should explicitly state your target price to anchor the negotiation and encourage the seller to make concessions.
When the seller has set a firm lowest price with conditions, avoid asking for additional items that the seller explicitly excludes, as it may not improve your negotiation position.

When the seller makes a small counteroffer close to your initial offer, avoid immediately accepting it without attempting further negotiation to maintain leverage and potentially secure a better price.
When the seller asserts the item is in perfect condition to justify a high price, you should question the condition to create leverage for negotiating a lower price.
When the seller states a firm price and confirms product quality, you should make a concrete cash offer with added assurances and willingness to meet promptly to encourage a price reduction.
When the seller has made a counteroffer slightly above your offer, you should propose a reasonable incremental concession to encourage agreement and close the deal.
When the seller agrees to a price that meets your target, you should confirm the deal promptly to finalize the negotiation and secure the favorable terms.
When the seller makes a clear counteroffer, avoid conceding prematurely without proposing a new counteroffer to maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller proposes a specific discounted price with a pickup deadline, you should accept the price and offer an earlier or convenient pickup time to increase the likelihood of closing the deal.

When the seller has made a reasonable counteroffer close to your initial target price, avoid immediately accepting it without attempting to negotiate further to maintain leverage and potentially secure a better deal.
When the seller makes a firm counteroffer slightly above your initial offer, avoid immediately accepting without attempting further negotiation to improve the price.
When the seller indicates willingness to negotiate and asks for your offer, you should directly propose your target price clearly and confidently to potentially secure the best deal quickly.
When the seller has already agreed to your proposed price, avoid making only polite acknowledgments without further negotiation or requests, as it does not improve your position.
When the seller has accepted your offer contingent on adding an item and arranging pickup, avoid focusing solely on logistics without reinforcing or negotiating price terms.
When the seller has agreed to a price contingent on additional trade-in items and immediate pickup, avoid delaying or hesitating to confirm your commitment to finalize the deal promptly.
When the seller invites offers indicating willingness to negotiate, you should make a low but reasonable initial offer to pressure the seller into lowering their price or making a counteroffer.
When the seller makes a conditional counteroffer with a specific price and terms, avoid immediately accepting without attempting to negotiate for a lower price or better conditions.
When the seller sets a firm lowest price but offers additional assurances, you should link your price acceptance to receiving those assurances to strengthen your negotiating position.
When the seller clearly states their lowest price and assures product authenticity, you should accept the offer to finalize the deal and secure a better price than the initial asking price.
When the seller expresses a firm initial price but shows willingness to negotiate after buyer concerns, you should raise legitimate doubts to prompt a price concession.
When the seller shows willingness to lower the price with conditions, you should make a slightly lower offer to secure a better deal while accommodating their terms.
When the seller has clearly stated their price, avoid immediately proposing a significantly lower offer without prior discussion, as it can weaken your negotiating position and reduce credibility.

When the seller maintains the original price and adds non-price incentives instead of lowering the price, avoid lowering your offer below your initial target price as it weakens your negotiation leverage.
When the seller responds to a buyer's increased offer by raising the price and adding conditions, avoid conceding too much too quickly as it weakens your negotiation leverage.
When the seller responds to a low offer with a counteroffer close to their original price, avoid making large concessions that strengthen the seller's position and reduce your negotiation leverage.
When the seller makes a firm but slightly flexible counteroffer close to their asking price, you should accept it to finalize a deal at a better price than the initial offer.
When the seller counters with a firm price, avoid accepting that price with non-price conditions that do not reduce the price, as it concedes leverage and weakens your negotiation position.
When the seller proposes a counteroffer between their initial price and your offer, you should make a lower offer to create downward pressure and encourage the seller to reduce their price further.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate but maintains a high price, you should use a personal emotional appeal combined with a clear budget and offer to barter to increase your leverage.
When the seller states their initial price but shows openness to offers, you should clearly state your target price to anchor the negotiation and encourage the seller to make a concession.
When the seller sets a firm counteroffer above the buyer's initial price, you should accept the offer conditionally to maintain negotiation momentum and ensure product verification.
When the seller states a firm initial price, you should make a lower offer combined with an immediate purchase incentive to encourage a more favorable counteroffer.
When the seller makes a reasonable counteroffer close to your target price, you should accept promptly to secure the deal and avoid risking losing the item.
When the seller prefers cash and has rejected a trade offer, avoid proposing trades that the seller considers incompatible or non-beneficial, as it may weaken your negotiation position.

When the seller proposes a compromise involving a partial cash payment and a trade-in, you should accept the offer promptly to secure a favorable deal and avoid risking higher prices through prolonged negotiation.
When the seller has already accepted your price offer and requested pickup, avoid delaying your confirmation to pick up, as it does not improve your negotiated price.
When the seller counters with a price close to their initial offer plus added value, avoid making offers significantly below your own stated target price as it may weaken your negotiating position.
When the seller offers a bundled item to justify a higher price, you should clarify and remove non-essential components to focus the negotiation on the main item's price.
When the seller has accepted a lower price contingent on specific pickup terms, you should confirm agreement promptly to finalize the deal efficiently.
When the seller firmly rejects a price significantly below both parties' initial offers, avoid lowering your offer drastically as it weakens your negotiation leverage and credibility.
When the seller maintains a firm price and provides only general information about the product's features, avoid asking for elaborations that do not create leverage for price negotiation.
When the seller firmly states a high asking price, you should justify your lower offer by referencing competitive alternatives and propose a specific, reasonable counteroffer.
When the seller has already conceded to a lower price, you should accept the agreed price promptly to finalize the deal efficiently and avoid unnecessary further negotiation.
When the seller states a high initial price, you should challenge it by setting a significantly lower target price to create downward pressure and encourage a substantial price concession.
When the seller has just reduced their price but not yet reached your target, you should directly request your ideal price to leverage their willingness to negotiate further.
When the seller offers a price reduction contingent on a trade-in, you should accept the trade-in condition and propose a specific lower price to strengthen your bargaining position.
When the seller makes a conditional price concession based on a trade-in, avoid simply acknowledging without confirming your ability to meet the condition or negotiating further to solidify the deal.
When the seller offers a lower price contingent on immediate pickup, you should confirm your ability to meet that condition to secure the better price.
When the buyer clearly states their maximum price, avoid immediately countering with a higher offer that disregards the buyer's stated limit and stalls negotiation progress.
When the seller has responded to price concerns by offering additional accessories, avoid only gathering information without leveraging these added values to negotiate a better price.
When the seller maintains a firm initial price but offers added accessories, you should make a reasonable counteroffer below their price to encourage a compromise with added value.
When the seller has bundled high-value accessories to justify a higher price, avoid asking questions that allow the seller to reinforce the increased price without directly negotiating a lower offer.
When the seller makes a counteroffer including added accessories at a price below their initial ask, avoid immediately accepting without attempting to negotiate further for a better deal.
When the seller firmly emphasizes the high quality and value of the item, avoid increasing your offer too quickly without gaining concessions, as it weakens your negotiating position.
When the seller insists on a high price due to item condition, you should propose a middle-ground offer that shows flexibility and highlights your unique preferences to encourage acceptance.
When the seller has accepted your highest offer without further negotiation, avoid simply confirming agreement without attempting to explore additional value or concessions.
When the seller has just lowered the price but added a condition, avoid making vague or non-specific statements that do not leverage the new offer to negotiate better terms.
When the seller offers a firm price contingent on immediate pickup, avoid accepting the price without negotiating or clarifying additional terms that may affect convenience or cost.
When the seller makes a clear counteroffer with specific conditions, you should accept the offer to secure a favorable deal and move the negotiation forward efficiently.
When the seller emphasizes the item's excellent condition without discussing price, avoid making vague expressions of interest that do not advance the negotiation toward a specific price discussion.
When the seller provides factual information about the item's condition, you should ask targeted questions to gather details that can justify negotiating a lower price.
When the seller confirms the product is in good condition without offering a price concession, avoid asking only informational questions that do not create leverage for a lower price.
When the seller confirms the price includes additional costs and offers extra value without lowering the base price, you should ask about included services or extras to increase overall deal value.
When the seller responds positively to product quality inquiries without conceding price flexibility, avoid asking questions that do not create leverage for lowering the price.
When the seller has made a firm counteroffer above your initial target price, avoid immediately accepting it without attempting further negotiation to maintain leverage and aim for a better deal.
